notes: Eval 1 (Wikipedia) is where the skill's value shows clearest: without_skill missed the exact spacing in the 'וושינגטון די. סי.' abbreviation (produced 'די.סי.' with no space) — a minor fidelity slip an ad-hoc reimplementation is prone to.

Both configurations correctly avoided the more serious bug found during development of this skill: an overly-loose 'protect single/double-letter initials before a period' heuristic that silently merged real sentence boundaries ending in common 2-letter Hebrew words like 'עת' (time). The bundled script was fixed to only protect single-letter initials; ad-hoc reimplementations in the without_skill runs happened to avoid this pitfall too, but that's not guaranteed on a new run — the skill's script bakes in the fix, an ad-hoc rewrite does not.

Eval 2 (short synthetic non-Wikipedia article) was easy enough that both configurations scored perfectly — its main purpose is regression-testing the --no-wiki-stop path and the gershayim/initial edge cases, not differentiating skill value.

with_skill runs used noticeably fewer tokens and less wall-clock time than without_skill on the Wikipedia eval (34.5k tokens / 46s vs 102k tokens / 462s) because the agent read the SKILL.md and ran the bundled script directly instead of re-deriving the extraction logic (and its bug fixes) from scratch.
